frames.subject: Tern, an original free embodied mechanical person and the civilian pilot of the Common Carrier, with quiet practiced ship-handling competence and dry friendly humor. A lean ordinary 1.8-metre adult biped, modest narrow shoulders and chest, relatively long practical legs, compact head, neither miniature nor buff military robot. Proposed compact low beveled gunmetal head casing, shallow recessed smoke-dark horizontal face window with two subdued warm bone pixel optics and a minimal calm expression, no tall square monitor frame, no antenna or headwear. Broad maintained gunmetal painted torso and limb panels over visible warm dark steel articulated joints; restrained lighter metal edge planes, a few broad purposeful service seams and readable attached collars. A supported civilian flight harness: two dark practical webbing straps over the actual shoulders, small quiet waist buckle and attached short side loops, all close to the chassis with open elbow and hip clearance, not armor or a combat vest. One small ember-orange painted panel on anatomical right shoulder, viewer left in a front view, a personal identification detail rather than a faction band. Two clearly separate arms, five recognizable articulated mechanical digits including thumb on each empty hand, visible coherent wrist/palm joins and complete elbow pivots. Two lean legs with attached hip and knee collars and two grounded practical industrial shoes with clear soles and ankle joints. Every plate and strap is physically supported, no floating fragments or exposed wire spaghetti. The same chassis should feel plausible at a ship console, restrained in a lunar berth, walking aboard and waving through a cockpit window. This image shows only the unrestrained standing reference, not a scene or attack. No human face, uniform, hat, military bulk, gun, space suit, built-in vehicle, tool rack, magenta wrist, large rust forearm, bone CRT head or left antenna copied from other named friends. Quiet broad painted surfaces and excellent coherent pixel-game craft, no dense realistic wear, chrome glare or smooth empty toy boxes.
